newsitem.title: FRANCE: ATHLETICS-KIPKETER SURPRISES HIMSELF WITH WORLD RECORD.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-KIPKETER SURPRISES HIMSELF WITH WORLD RECORD.

text.p: Wilson Kipketer of Denmark surprised even himself by crushing the eight-year-old 800 metres indoor world record with a time of one minute 43.96 seconds at the indoor world championships on Friday.
"It was not my plan to demolish the field or the record," said Kipketer after breaking the previous best mark of 1:44.84 set by Paul Ereng of Kenya in March 1989 in Budapest.
Kenyan-born Kipketer was in a class of his own as he won his first-round race with astonishing ease and set a world record which will earn him a $50,000 cheque.
"I just wanted to get the heat finished without any problems," he said. "The record is a bonus."
The 26-year-old Kipketer, who lives in Denmark, was not allowed to take part in last year's Atlanta Olympics as he was awaiting Danish citizenship at the time.
